MEM.note:
Not compiled, not tested, nothing run, per the phase rules. src/ir/mod.rs did not exist yet, so the imports point at the IR submodules the contract lists (types, value, inst, func, module). Cargo.toml is unchanged: there are no new dependencies, and the hashing reuses crate::psa::bdd::fxhash.

What is not covered:
(1) Contexts are k = 1 only (1-call-site or 1-object, optionally with the same context on heap objects). There is no deeper k.
(2) Calls back from external code only reach methods that override external declarations the TypeHierarchy knows about, plus closures that reach the external world. Reflection, dynamic proxies and dependency-injection frameworks are modelled only as calls to external code.
(3) Field-sensitivity assumes well-typed field access. In the C family, the content slot (`*p`) and the field slots (`p->f`) are separate cells, so union and type-punning overlap is not modelled. AliasOracle does report content-slot accesses as MayAlias with every slot. Pointer arithmetic keeps the base object, and array elements share one summarized slot.
(4) An ownership part only counts as owner-made when it is allocated in the same function that stores it, or comes back from a callee that always returns fresh objects. A part passed through a setter (`this.setX(new X())`) is therefore classified as aggregation or association, not composition.
(5) GlobalIr has no initializers. Global initial values must be lowered as ModuleInit/StaticInit functions, which are always seeded as entry points.
(6) MustAlias is only reported for the same SSA value or a static-storage object that exists once.
(7) The defaults are OpenWorld entry points with the sound external policy (sound but imprecise); the ReturnUnknownOnly policy is an explicit unsound assumption that the result records. For useful precision, the project model must supply Explicit entry points and the frontends must supply hierarchy, intrinsic and spawn facts.

CSFE.note:
Grammar and API: I wrote against the Cargo.toml that is on disk now: tree-sitter 0.25 and tree-sitter-c-sharp 0.23, using `tree_sitter_c_sharp::LANGUAGE.into()`. Node kinds come from v0.23.1 node-types.json. My earlier edit adding a "0.20.0" dependency line was replaced by the owner's upgrade, which already includes `tree-sitter-c-sharp = "0.23"`, so Cargo.toml needs no further change. The C and Kotlin frontends still call the old 0.20 `language()` function and will not build against this Cargo.toml.

Phase 1 (ingest.rs): it maps every token kind the grammar produces. `identifier` is treated as a single token, so keywords like `var` or `from` used as names come out as Identifier. String and character literals are single tokens; interpolated strings keep the tokens of the code inside `{...}`. `///` comments are doc comments. ERROR and MISSING nodes are counted by the shared walker, not by the adapter.

Phase 2 (reduce.rs): every node kind the grammar defines is classified. ERROR nodes are removed but their children kept, MISSING nodes are dropped, and both, plus any unknown kind, are counted in `stats()`. All listed modifiers and the five C# access levels (plus `file`) go into the NodeAttr word. `CSharpModifiers::of` returns the full modifier set straight from the syntax tree.

Contract decisions:
- Variable declarators are NN_LOCAL_VAR_DECL, because the current ast.rs removed NN_VAR_DECLARATOR.
- NN_YIELD_STMT is reused because it already exists; yield break sets aux bit 0, matching neutral.rs.
- foreach uses NN_FOREACH_STMT, the name in the contract and neutral.rs, not the existing NN_ENHANCED_FOR.

Not covered or lossy:
1. The grammar hides the `params` array rule, so `params T[] xs` becomes a TYPE_REF followed by a PARAM_DECL leaf for the name.
2. `with { ... }` initializers and anonymous-type members are positional name/value pairs.
3. Code in every `#if`/`#else` branch is reduced, which can produce duplicate declarations; directive conditions are dropped.
4. Nested deconstruction such as `var (a, (b, c))` is flattened.
5. These are not stored in the NodeAttr word: `new`, `unsafe` and `file` on members, `checked` on explicit conversions, query ascending/descending, and interpolation alignment/format. They can still be read from the syntax tree.
6. C# switch has no fall-through; this relies on the C# control-flow rules (`switch_fall_through = false`) set by whoever owns the Phase 3/CFG language rules.
